## Instructions

## Question 1 

In the study of gifted children, researchers tested whether the average IQ of mothers of gifted children differs from the general population mean of 100. The sample mean was 118.2 with a standard error of 1.083.

What is the correct interpretation of a very small p-value (e.g., ≈ 0) in this context?

A. We can be sure that the population mean is 118.2.  
B. The observed sample mean must be incorrect.  
C. The data provide strong evidence against the null hypothesis that the mean is 100.  
D. The study has a large effect size.  
E. The data are too variable to draw conclusions.

---

## Question 1 - Correct Answer

In the study of gifted children, researchers tested whether the average IQ of mothers of gifted children differs from the general population mean of 100. The sample mean was 118.2 with a standard error of 1.083.

What is the correct interpretation of a very small p-value (e.g., ≈ 0) in this context?

A. We can be sure that the population mean is 118.2.  
B. The observed sample mean must be incorrect.  
✅ C. The data provide strong evidence against the null hypothesis that the mean is 100.  
D. The study has a large effect size.  
E. The data are too variable to draw conclusions.

## Question 2 

What conditions must hold to safely use the normal model to approximate the sampling distribution of a sample mean?

A. A large population and small margin of error.  
B. A non-random sample and n > 100.  
C. Independence of observations and either n ≥ 30 or population not strongly skewed.  
D. Equal variances in the population.  
E. A sample mean close to the population mean.

---

## Question 2 - Correct Answer

What conditions must hold to safely use the normal model to approximate the sampling distribution of a sample mean?

A. A large population and small margin of error.  
B. A non-random sample and n > 100.  
✅ C. Independence of observations and either n ≥ 30 or population not strongly skewed.  
D. Equal variances in the population.  
E. A sample mean close to the population mean.

## Question 3 

Which of the following is **not** a valid null hypothesis?

A. The average hours of cat sleep is 14 hours.  
B. The sample mean of cat sleep is 16 hours.  
C. There is no difference in average sleep between cats and dogs.  
D. μ = 14  
E. The population proportion is 0.25.

---

## Question 3 - Correct Answer

Which of the following is **not** a valid null hypothesis?

A. The average hours of cat sleep is 14 hours.  
✅ B. The sample mean of cat sleep is 16 hours.  
C. There is no difference in average sleep between cats and dogs.  
D. μ = 14  
E. The population proportion is 0.25.

## Question 4 

The Central Limit Theorem tells us that:

A. The sample mean will always be normally distributed.  
B. Larger samples will have larger standard errors.  
C. The sampling distribution of the mean will be nearly normal if sample size is large enough.  
D. Confidence intervals are always accurate.  
E. Sample means are always equal to population means.

---

## Question 4 - Correct Answer

The Central Limit Theorem tells us that:

A. The sample mean will always be normally distributed.  
B. Larger samples will have larger standard errors.  
✅ C. The sampling distribution of the mean will be nearly normal if sample size is large enough.  
D. Confidence intervals are always accurate.  
E. Sample means are always equal to population means.

## Question 5

A. Males and females have equal qualifications.  
B. The resume was not manipulated.  
C. There is bias in the decision process.  
D. Promotion decisions are independent of gender.  
E. The difference in proportions is real.

## Question 6 

Which statement about Type I and Type II errors is correct?

A. Type I error is failing to reject a false null hypothesis.  
B. Type I error is rejecting a true null hypothesis.  
C. Type II error is rejecting a false null hypothesis.  
D. Type II error means your sample size is too small.  
E. Power = probability of making a Type I error.

---

## Question 6 - Correct Answer

Which statement about Type I and Type II errors is correct?

A. Type I error is failing to reject a false null hypothesis.  
✅ B. Type I error is rejecting a true null hypothesis.  
C. Type II error is rejecting a false null hypothesis.  
D. Type II error means your sample size is too small.  
E. Power = probability of making a Type I error.

---

## Question 7 

Which scenario **illustrates** statistical significance but not practical significance?

A. A study finds a large effect size with p < 0.05.  
B. A huge sample finds a 0.1 point GPA difference with p < 0.001.  
C. A small sample fails to reject H₀.  
D. The confidence interval is wide.  
E. A new method doubles graduation rates.

---

## Question 8 

When a confidence interval for a population mean **does not contain the null value**, what does that suggest?

A. Reject the null hypothesis.  
B. Fail to reject the null hypothesis.  
C. The standard error is too small.  
D. The sample is not random.  
E. Increase your alpha level.

---

## Question 8 - Correct Answer

When a confidence interval for a population mean **does not contain the null value**, what does that suggest?

✅ A. Reject the null hypothesis.  
B. Fail to reject the null hypothesis.  
C. The standard error is too small.  
D. The sample is not random.  
E. Increase your alpha level.

A. We lower the significance level.

C. The population is smaller.  
D. The sample size increases.  
E. The standard deviation increases.

## Question 9 - Correct Answer

## Question 10 

Which pair correctly links hypothesis testing and confidence intervals?

A. α = 0.05 → 99% confidence level  
B. α = 0.05 two-sided test → 95% confidence level  
C. α = 0.05 one-sided test → 95% confidence level  
D. CI excludes 0 → fail to reject H₀  
E. CI includes H₀ → reject the null

---

## Question 10 - Correct Answer

Which pair correctly links hypothesis testing and confidence intervals?

A. α = 0.05 → 99% confidence level  
✅ B. α = 0.05 two-sided test → 95% confidence level  
C. α = 0.05 one-sided test → 95% confidence level  
D. CI excludes 0 → fail to reject H₀  
E. CI includes H₀ → reject the null
